Name: One tool for every ecosystem
Requirement: The system shall be one command-line tool, analog-attach, for every ecosystem; the ecosystem a project uses is a setting of that project.

Name: Same command, same meaning
Requirement: A command with the same name shall do the same kind of thing in every ecosystem, so that a user who knows one ecosystem can work in another.

Name: Commands of the selected ecosystem
Requirement: Commands, flags and settings that apply to only one ecosystem shall be offered (in help and completion) only when that ecosystem is selected.

Name: Use without interactive questions
Requirement: Every operation shall be possible without interactive questions, so that the tool can be driven from scripts, the UI and the AI skill.

Name: Questions only on a terminal
Requirement: The system shall ask questions only when it runs on a terminal and --json is not given; otherwise it shall report what it would have asked.

Name: Stopping a question
Requirement: Stopping an interactive question (Ctrl+C) shall end the command and keep every answer already given.

Name: Machine-readable output
Requirement: Every command shall accept --json, anywhere on the command line, and then print one JSON result instead of text.

Name: Consistent results and errors
Requirement: Every JSON result shall say whether the command succeeded, with a message and a severity, in the same structure in every ecosystem.

Name: Error types
Requirement: Every error and warning shall carry a type from a fixed list (the Error types tab), the same in every ecosystem, so that scripts and the UI can tell them apart; the message says which case it is.
Source (internal): request 2026-10-29; Linux config errors have kind today

Name: Exit status
Requirement: The exit status shall be 0 whenever the command ran, its outcome being in the result; a non-zero status shall mean a usage error (unknown command, bad argument) or a failure of the tool itself.

Name: Help
Requirement: analog-attach --help shall list the commands, and analog-attach <command> --help shall describe the command, its arguments and flags, with examples.

Name: Version
Requirement: analog-attach --version shall print the version of the tool.

Name: Explain and point onward
Requirement: When a command cannot be carried out, the message shall say why and, where it is known, what to do next (the command or setting that fixes it, or the closest valid name for a mistyped one).

Name: Missing settings
Requirement: A command that needs a setting with no value shall stop before doing anything and name the setting and how to set it.

Name: Naming a device
Requirement: Commands that act on a device in the workfile shall take it as a target.

Name: Naming a device in CAPI
Requirement: In CAPI, a target shall be the device's name.

Name: Naming a node in Linux
Requirement: In Linux, a target shall be a label (spi0), an absolute path (/soc/spi@7e204000), or a label followed by a path (spi0/adc@0).

Name: Edits are saved at once
Requirement: A command that changes the workfile shall save it before it returns; commands that only show something shall never change the workfile or the settings.

Name: Guided setup
Requirement: Run with no arguments on a terminal, the system shall walk the user through the settings a project needs, starting with the ecosystem, and then offer to create the workfile (analog-attach init).

Name: Keep what is set
Requirement: The guided setup shall ask only for settings that have no value, and shall save each answer as soon as it is given, so that it can be stopped and resumed.

Name: Offer the choices
Requirement: Where the possible values are known (ecosystems, boards, base device trees), the guided setup shall offer them to pick from rather than ask the user to type them.

Name: Without a terminal
Requirement: With --quiet, with --json, or without a terminal, analog-attach with no arguments shall ask nothing: it shall show the help and say which required settings are still missing.

Name: Next steps
Requirement: At the end of the guided setup the system shall say what to do next: find a device (analog-attach list devices) and add it (analog-attach add).

Name: Show every setting
Requirement: analog-attach config shall list the settings of the selected ecosystem, grouped by category, with each value, where it comes from (project, user, default or unset) and which are required.

Name: Show one setting
Requirement: analog-attach config <key> shall show that setting's value, what it is for, and the values it can take where they are known.

Name: Change a setting
Requirement: analog-attach config <key> <value> shall set that setting, refusing a value it cannot take (not one of its choices, a path that does not exist) with the reason.

Name: Reset a setting
Requirement: With --reset, the setting shall go back to its default, or to unset when it has none.

Name: User and project settings
Requirement: Settings shall be kept for the user and for a project, the project's value winning; the project settings are found from the current directory upward.

Name: Where a change goes
Requirement: A change shall go to the project settings when the project has them, and to the user settings otherwise; with --local it shall go to the project settings, creating them in the current directory if there are none.

Name: Rebuild the caches
Requirement: analog-attach config --reload shall rebuild what the ecosystem caches from its sources, and say so when the ecosystem caches nothing.

Name: Linux caches
Requirement: In Linux, --reload shall rebuild the binding index and the validation data from the Linux tree.

Name: Caches follow the sources
Requirement: Changing a setting that points to the ecosystem's sources (Linux: the Linux tree) shall rebuild the caches built from them, saying that it takes time.

Name: One setting at a time
Requirement: analog-attach config shall show or change one setting per call.

Name: Setting names
Requirement: Setting names shall use one style (kebab-case), and the settings shall be stored as JSON.

Name: Unknown setting
Requirement: An unknown setting name shall be refused, naming the closest setting.

Name: Ecosystem
Requirement: The ecosystem setting shall select the ecosystem (Linux or CAPI) of the project, and be stored with the project so that projects on one machine can differ.

Name: Linux sources and target
Requirement: In Linux, the linux setting shall name the Linux tree and the devicetree setting the base .dts of the board the overlay is for; both are required.

Name: Linux output options
Requirement: In Linux, overlay-syntax shall choose how the overlay is written (fragments, the default, or labels), and preprocess-command the C preprocessor run on device trees.

Name: CAPI sources
Requirement: In CAPI, capi-path shall name the CAPI tree (required) and module-paths the extra module trees (drivers, platforms), as a path list.

Name: CAPI target
Requirement: In CAPI, one target setting shall name what the project is for: a board, or a platform (chip) used without a board; a board brings its platform with it.

Name: CAPI project
Requirement: In CAPI, project-name and project-path shall say where the generated project goes, project-template which template set renders it (default capi), and example whether example code is included (default on).

Name: Questions after an edit
Requirement: The interview setting (default on) shall turn on or off the questions for what is left to set after an edit.

Name: Filling after an edit
Requirement: In CAPI, the bootstrap setting (default on) shall turn on or off the automatic filling of values after an edit.

Name: Own build and deploy
Requirement: The build-command and deploy-command settings shall replace the ecosystem's own build or deploy step with a command of the user's.

Name: Build folder
Requirement: The build-dir setting shall name the folder analog-attach build writes to and analog-attach deploy takes the output from, so that a project can keep several builds side by side.
Source (internal): request 2026-10-29: implement in CAPI as well

Name: CAPI deploy target
Requirement: In CAPI, the probe setting shall name the debug probe used to flash: openocd (the default) or jlink.

Name: Linux deploy target
Requirement: In Linux, the deploy-ip, deploy-user and deploy-password settings shall name the remote device and the login used to reach it.

Name: Create the workfile
Requirement: analog-attach init shall create an empty workfile at the path the workfile setting names, for the configured target.

Name: CAPI workfile
Requirement: In CAPI, the workfile shall be for the board or platform the target setting names.

Name: Linux workfile
Requirement: In Linux, the workfile shall be an empty overlay for the base device tree the devicetree setting names.

Name: Never overwrite
Requirement: analog-attach init shall never overwrite an existing workfile; when the file exists, it shall leave it as it is and say so.

Name: Missing settings
Requirement: When settings it needs are missing, analog-attach init shall name them and point to analog-attach config, or to analog-attach with no arguments for the guided setup.

Name: No questions
Requirement: analog-attach init shall never ask questions: the guided setup is analog-attach with no arguments.

Name: Report
Requirement: analog-attach init shall report the workfile's path and whether it was created.

Name: Linux caches
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach init shall check that the binding caches are built and, if not, say how to build them.

Name: Devices that can be added
Requirement: analog-attach list devices shall list every device type that can be added to the workfile, each with the key analog-attach add takes.

Name: Filter
Requirement: With a filter, analog-attach list devices shall keep the device types whose key contains it.

Name: CAPI grouping
Requirement: In CAPI, analog-attach list devices shall group the device types by kind: evaluation boards, drivers, and the types of each module.

Name: Linux grouping
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach list devices shall list compatible strings, grouped by category.

Name: Possible targets
Requirement: analog-attach list context shall list the targets a project can be set up for.

Name: CAPI targets
Requirement: In CAPI, analog-attach list context shall list the platforms, each with the boards that carry it, as the target setting takes them.

Name: Linux targets
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach list context shall list the .dts files of the Linux tree, as the devicetree setting takes them.

Name: Picking a target
Requirement: analog-attach list context shall say how to select one of the targets it lists.

Name: Properties of a device
Requirement: analog-attach list property shall list the devices of the workfile; given a target, its properties, each with its type and whether it is required and set.

Name: Values for a property
Requirement: analog-attach list value shall list the values a property can take, and whether a new device can be created to fill it.

Name: Union members
Requirement: In CAPI, for a union property, naming a member shall list that member's values.

Name: Where a device can go
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach list parent shall list the buses or nodes of the base tree a device type can be placed under.

Name: Existing overlays for a device
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach list overlay shall list the overlays of the Linux tree that contain the device type, and whether each fits the board.

Name: Unknown kind
Requirement: An unknown kind shall be refused, listing the kinds the selected ecosystem offers: devices, context, property and value in every ecosystem.

Name: Linux kinds
Requirement: In Linux, the kinds shall also include parent and overlay.

Name: Add a device
Requirement: analog-attach add <key> shall add a device of the type the key names (from analog-attach list devices) to the workfile, and report the name it was given.

Name: Unknown device type
Requirement: An unknown key shall be refused, naming the closest keys.

Name: Name
Requirement: --name shall name the new device; without it the system shall pick a name that is not taken. A taken or invalid name shall be refused.

Name: CAPI default name
Requirement: In CAPI, a default name shall be a C identifier made from the part and its role (adxl355_spi_device), or the device type numbered (gpio0).

Name: Linux default name
Requirement: In Linux, the default name shall be the compatible with its unit address (adc@0).

Name: Add a part by name
Requirement: In CAPI, the key may also be a driver (adxl355) or an evaluation board: the system shall then add the device handle the part is used through, with what it needs.

Name: Choose interfaces
Requirement: In CAPI, for a driver with several interfaces (ad74413r: adc, dac), --as shall choose which to add, several being given comma-separated for one chip.

Name: Parent
Requirement: In Linux, --parent shall place the device under that node; without it the device shall go under the first valid parent, with a note saying which.

Name: Ask for the parent
Requirement: In Linux, on a terminal and without --parent, the system shall first ask for the parent, offering the valid ones.

Name: Label
Requirement: In Linux, --label shall set the new node's label; without it a label shall be generated.

Name: Start from an example
Requirement: In Linux, --template shall choose what the node starts from: only its required properties (the default), an example of its binding (example:N), or an overlay of the Linux tree (overlay:name).

Name: Fill what leaves no choice
Requirement: In CAPI, after an add, the system shall fill in every value that leaves no choice (bootstrap), and report what it filled and what is left for the user.

Name: Ask for what is left
Requirement: After an add, on a terminal, the system shall ask for the required values still missing, one at a time, offering the possible values where known (interview); each answer shall be saved at once.

Name: Quiet
Requirement: With --quiet, the system shall not ask: it shall list the required values still missing instead.

Name: Completion
Requirement: analog-attach add shall complete device keys and flag values on the command line where the shell supports it.

Name: Start from an existing design
Requirement: analog-attach import <path> shall start a new workfile from an existing design, refusing to overwrite a workfile that already exists.

Name: Import a Linux overlay
Requirement: In Linux, the path may be an overlay of the Linux tree (by name, from analog-attach list overlay) or any overlay file; its fragments shall be imported as written, and the RPi overlay parameters dropped.

Name: What does not fit
Requirement: In Linux, targets and references that the base device tree does not have shall be reported as warnings, with whether the overlay fits the board.

Name: The imported workfile
Requirement: In Linux, the new workfile shall be named after the overlay and become the configured one; the previous workfile shall be kept.

Name: Import a CAPI workfile
Requirement: In CAPI, the path shall be a workfile, copied to the configured workfile path after checking that it loads with the configured modules.

Name: Whole workfile
Requirement: analog-attach read with no arguments shall show the whole workfile.

Name: One device
Requirement: analog-attach read <target> shall show that device with its properties, and the required properties it still lacks.

Name: Linux subtree
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach read <target> shall also show the node's children.

Name: One property
Requirement: analog-attach read <target> <property> shall show the property's value, what it is for, its type and allowed values, its default, and who set it (the user or the system).

Name: Suggestions
Requirement: When reading a property, the system shall also show the values it suggests for it, and whether a new device can be created to fill it.

Name: Values only
Requirement: With --quiet, analog-attach read shall print only the values, without descriptions or suggestions, so that the output can be used in scripts.

Name: Base and overlay
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach read shall show the base device tree and the overlay together, marking what comes from the base.

Name: Where a device comes from
Requirement: In JSON, each device shall say whether it is the user's (internal) or comes from the target (external), and list its other names.

Name: Set a property
Requirement: analog-attach update shall set a property of a device to the value given; a value may span several arguments.

Name: Refuse what the definition does not allow
Requirement: The system shall refuse, with the reason, a value or a property the device's definition does not allow.

Name: No value
Requirement: Without a value, analog-attach update shall show the property, as analog-attach read does.

Name: Flag properties
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach update without a value, for a property the node does not have, shall set it as a flag (a property with no value).

Name: What it can be set to
Requirement: With --suggest, analog-attach update shall list the values the property can take instead of setting it.

Name: Quiet
Requirement: With --quiet, when analog-attach update shows a property it shall print only the value, and when it creates a device it shall list what is missing instead of asking.

Name: CAPI values
Requirement: In CAPI, a union shall take its member and value ('member,value' or two arguments), an array a comma-separated list, and a reference the name of another device; the leading $ of a property name may be left out.

Name: Linux values
Requirement: In Linux, a value shall be written as in device tree source: numbers, macros (GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW), references (&spi0), strings, arrays as several tokens, and matrices with rows separated by commas.

Name: Create a child node
Requirement: In Linux, naming a child that does not exist instead of a property shall create that child node, then ask for its missing required properties on a terminal.

Name: Unit address follows reg
Requirement: In Linux, changing reg shall also change the node's unit address to match.

Name: Fill after a change
Requirement: In CAPI, after an update, the system shall again fill the values that now leave no choice, and report them.

Name: Remove a property
Requirement: analog-attach delete <target> <property> shall remove the property's value.

Name: CAPI property
Requirement: In CAPI, the property shall go back to its default, or to unset when it has none.

Name: Linux property
Requirement: In Linux, the property shall be removed from the node.

Name: Remove a device
Requirement: analog-attach delete <target> shall remove the device; when the removal would also affect other devices (references, children), the system shall show what would change and remove nothing unless --force is given.

Name: Remove everything
Requirement: analog-attach delete with no arguments shall show what would be removed, and remove every device only with --force.

Name: Only what the user added
Requirement: In Linux, only nodes and properties of the overlay shall be removable; the base device tree is never changed.

Name: Same in text and JSON
Requirement: --force shall behave the same with and without --json.

Name: Fill after a removal
Requirement: In CAPI, after a delete, the system shall fill again the values that now leave no choice, and report what is left.

Name: Rename a device
Requirement: analog-attach rename shall give a device a new name, refusing a name that is taken or not valid in the ecosystem.

Name: Keep references
Requirement: Renaming a device shall update every reference to it.

Name: Unit address
Requirement: In Linux, a new name without @ shall keep the unit address; a name with @ shall change it and update reg to match.

Name: Move a device
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach move shall move a node of the overlay under another parent, which may be a node of the base device tree.

Name: Only valid parents
Requirement: Moving a node under a parent its binding does not allow shall be refused, naming the valid parents.

Name: Switch a device on or off
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach enable and analog-attach disable shall switch a node on or off (status okay or disabled), for nodes of the overlay and of the base device tree.

Name: CAPI later
Requirement: In CAPI, switching a device on or off without removing it is a possible later addition, not required now.

Name: Check the workfile
Requirement: analog-attach validate shall check the whole workfile against the definitions of its devices and report each problem with the device and property it concerns.

Name: Errors and warnings
Requirement: Each problem shall be an error (the output cannot be built) or a warning, and the result shall say whether there are errors.

Name: CAPI checks
Requirement: In CAPI, analog-attach validate shall check the rules of the device definitions: required values, allowed values and references to other devices.

Name: Linux checks
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach validate shall check the overlay merged with the base device tree against the bindings, and report overlapping addresses.

Name: Generate the project
Requirement: In CAPI, analog-attach generate shall render the workfile into a project that builds: to project-path, or out/<project-name> when it is unset.

Name: Where
Requirement: --output shall write the project to another directory for this run.

Name: Which templates
Requirement: --project-template shall choose the template set for this run, a name or a path (default: the project-template setting).

Name: Keep the user's own code
Requirement: Generating the project again shall not overwrite the user's own code (the application source).

Name: Build the output
Requirement: analog-attach build shall build the ecosystem's output.

Name: CAPI build
Requirement: In CAPI, analog-attach build shall build the generated project into a firmware image.

Name: Linux build
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach build shall compile the overlay into a .dtbo.

Name: Report missing prerequisites
Requirement: Before building, the system shall check what the build needs (the project was generated, the tools are installed) and report what is missing.

Name: Report where the output is
Requirement: analog-attach build shall report where the built output is, in the same form in every ecosystem.

Name: Clean build
Requirement: In CAPI, --clean shall remove the previous build output first, so that the build starts fresh.

Name: Separate from generate
Requirement: analog-attach build shall not generate the project; generate and build stay two commands.

Name: Build failures
Requirement: When the build fails, the system shall show the build tool's messages and say that it failed.

Name: Put it on the hardware
Requirement: analog-attach deploy shall put the built output on the target hardware, and say first how to build it when it is missing.

Name: CAPI: flash the board
Requirement: In CAPI, analog-attach deploy shall flash the board through a debug probe; --probe (openocd or jlink) shall override the probe setting for this run.

Name: Linux: copy and reboot
Requirement: In Linux, analog-attach deploy shall copy the .dtbo to the remote device's overlay directory and reboot it, using the deploy-ip and deploy-user settings.

Name: Print the script
Requirement: analog-attach completion shall print the completion script for bash, fish or zsh, for the shell given or the user's own shell by default.

Name: Install it
Requirement: --install shall install the script for the user, where the shell loads it by itself, replacing an earlier one and never editing a shell startup file.

Name: Remove it
Requirement: --uninstall shall remove the installed script.

Name: What it completes
Requirement: Completion shall offer commands, flags, setting names and values, device types, device names, properties and property values, from the same source as analog-attach list.

Name: Install the AI-assistant skill
Requirement: analog-attach skill install shall install the skill that teaches Claude Code to use the tool for an ecosystem, refusing to replace an installed copy unless --force is given.

Name: Remove it
Requirement: analog-attach skill uninstall shall remove an installed skill.

Name: One skill per ecosystem
Requirement: There shall be a skill per ecosystem (linux, capi), named on the command line.
